title: Historical construction example: a glossed word family in Hildegard's Lingua ignota
task: Inspect an actual medieval invented vocabulary or script for a concrete learnable convention and its costs. No Voynich theory, source identity, native word value, corpus acquisition or experiment is proposed.

concrete_construction_observation.directly_attested: The father and mother pairs have the same extra initial string nilz- before two unchanged different base words, and the Latin glosses supply the same corresponding step-kinship distinction. The entries are neighboring members of a semantically organized list. This is stronger source evidence for a reusable piece than an unglossed resemblance between invented strings.
concrete_construction_observation.bounded_human_rule_inference: For these two attested pairs, a reader can learn the two bases and the shared addition rather than four unrelated whole forms: choose the father or mother base and prefix nilz-. That is a concise reconstruction of the observed pattern. The manuscript does not explicitly instruct the scribe to apply this rule to all kinship words, and this note does not claim that we have recovered Hildegard's actual word-invention algorithm.
concrete_construction_observation.retained_countercase: The immediately following son/stepson pair is not exact prefixation of the complete listed son form: nilz- plus Scirizin would retain its final in, whereas the listed compound is Nilzsciriz. A stem alternation, lexicalized compound or other explanation would therefore have to be paid. It is not permissible to declare every long word simple prefix-plus-unchanged-base on the strength of the first two pairs.
concrete_construction_observation.what_differs_from_a_free_program_grammar: The actual evidence is a taught/consultable lexicon with semantically adjacent word families and explicit glosses, plus some transparent reuse and retained whole-form differences. There is no observed per-character state counter, full-message ID or freely assigned output word in this observation. Vocabulary organization itself carries a real learning and lookup cost; a small affix does not eliminate the many remaining lexical entries.
concrete_construction_observation.what_it_does_not_supply: No complete invented-language syntax, productive treatment of arbitrary new names, sentence-boundary convention, negation scope or open-text inverse is established by these two glossary pages. The separate invented alphabet does not supply those missing linguistic rules. A proposed full writer would have to state them independently and could not cite this glossary as evidence that they were historical.

costs_and_research_consequence.learning: At least the two selected base meanings and the shared relationship need to be learned; the son pair already adds an irregular-form obligation if included. The broader vocabulary remains a substantial learned or written reference resource, not a small free primitive table. The alphabet table adds a different learning task if used.
costs_and_research_consequence.manual_use: A scribe can copy or consult neighboring kinship entries. Analogical prefixation works exactly for the two cited bases. Actual speed, teaching practice, memorization and use in ordinary prose are not measured or proved.
costs_and_research_consequence.useful_design_constraint: When inventing a source-side technical language, preserve a mixture of semantically organized lexical bases, constrained productive additions and explicitly learned exceptions. Do not assume that a historically plausible invented language must be generated from29universal roots, or that a thousand-entry glossary proves an arbitrary large cipher table costless.
costs_and_research_consequence.not_a_test_selection: This is a historical construction example only. No new full writer, native hypothesis, selected source, statistical prediction or experiment follows automatically. The old source-frequency failures remain unchanged.
